questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Time for one circle in a magnetic field
questions.learningObjective: Explain why the period is independent of speed
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook asks why the time for one circle in a magnetic field does not depend on the charge's speed.

answer.exemplar: The period T = 2 pi m/(qB) contains no speed term; although a faster charge has a larger radius, it also travels faster, and these two effects cancel exactly.

questions.explanation: T = 2 pi m/(qB) is independent of v because r grows with v while circumference grows with r. A tempting error is to assume faster means shorter period.

questions.topic: Time for one circle in a magnetic field
questions.learningObjective: State that period is independent of speed
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook asks which quantity does NOT affect the period of a charge's circular motion in a uniform magnetic field.

options.text: The magnetic field, because stronger field means shorter period
The mass of the charge, because heavier means longer period
The speed of the charge, because T = 2 pi m/(qB)
The charge, because larger charge means shorter period

questions.explanation: T = 2 pi m/(qB) depends on mass, charge and field but not speed. Speed changes radius, not period.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Critical angle at a glass to air boundary
questions.learningObjective: Explain total internal reflection
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook asks why total internal reflection cannot occur when light goes from air into glass.

answer.exemplar: Total internal reflection requires travel from a denser to a rarer medium; air to glass is rarer to denser, so the refracted ray always exists and no critical angle applies.

questions.explanation: The condition n1 > n2 is not met for air to glass. A tempting error is to compute a critical angle anyway.

questions.learningObjective: State the dependence of wire force on angle
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook asks how the force on a current-carrying wire depends on the angle between the wire and the field.

options.text: It varies as cos theta, maximum when parallel
It varies as sin theta, from zero parallel to maximum perpendicular
It is constant, independent of angle
It varies as tan theta, unbounded

questions.explanation: F = B I L sin theta, so it is zero when parallel and maximum when perpendicular. Cosine would give the opposite behaviour.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Magnetic force at an angle to the field
questions.learningObjective: Explain why force is maximum perpendicular
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook asks why the magnetic force on a charge is greatest when it moves perpendicular to the field.

answer.exemplar: The force magnitude is F = q v B sin theta, and sin theta reaches its maximum value of 1 at theta = 90 degrees, so perpendicular motion gives the greatest force.

questions.explanation: sin90 = 1 is the maximum of sine. A tempting error is to think faster parallel motion could beat it.
questions.hint: sin theta is maximum at 90 degrees.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Radius of the circular path of a charge
questions.learningObjective: Interpret a table of mass versus radius

stimulus.body: A beekeeper logged radius for fixed v and B: m=1.67 x10^-27 kg gives r=0.0835 m; m=3.34 x10^-27 gives r=0.167 m; m=6.68 x10^-27 gives r=0.334 m.

questions.stem: From the log, what is r for m = 9.11 x10^-31 kg under the same conditions? Use v = 2.0 x10^6 m/s, B = 0.10 T, q = 1.6 x10^-19 C.

options.text: 5.69 x10^-5 m, halving the result
2.28 x10^-4 m, doubling the result
1.14 x10^-4 m, from r = mv/(qB)
0.0835 m, reading the first row

questions.explanation: r = mv/(qB) = (9.11 x10^-31)(2.0 x10^6)/((1.6 x10^-19)(0.10)) = 1.14 x10^-4 m. The table confirms linearity in mass.
